main_mystery: Does the machine foresee, or choose?
truth: The machine is not prophetic. It prints the name of the patient Iris Callahan will unknowingly let die through a clinical decision that night. It reflects her hand, not the future. The machine responds to her choices, not fate.

red_herrings.description: The machine is a supernatural entity or ghost that can predict the future.
The machine is a warning system from the future that can be outrun if Iris acts fast enough.
The machine is cursed by the hospital's past or connected to a malevolent force.

major_reveals.description: Every name printed so far corresponds to a patient Iris personally triaged. Marguerite mutters: 'It only ever prints your handwriting.'
Marguerite's old logbook reveals the same machine 30 years ago with the same pattern; she quit nursing rather than confront the truth.

The machine reflects Iris's choices: when she does nothing, no slip is fulfilled. It prints the name of the person she will let die by her clinical decision. It named last year's death too — she had a choice.
The machine prints IRIS CALLAHAN with a time. Iris stops fighting, accepts the death she cannot prevent, and burns the machine. The loop is broken.

clues.description: First slip prints 'Lena' and '03:47' before the girl arrives. Iris discards it; the child arrives at 03:12.
clues.note: Establishes the machine's pattern; later understood as Iris's own triage decision that will lead to the predicted outcome.

clues.description: Marguerite Vole: 'It only ever prints your handwriting.'
clues.note: First hint that the machine is tied to Iris personally, not fate.

clues.description: Marguerite's old logbook shows the same machine 30 years ago, same pattern: each slip matched a patient the nurse triaged. She quit nursing afterward.
clues.note: Confirms historical consistency and that the machine's behavior repeats with a different nurse.

clues.description: Iris does nothing, lets a night pass by protocol — no slip is fulfilled. Evidence that the machine responds to her choices.
clues.note: Direct evidence that the machine is not fate-based; it reflects her inaction.

clues.description: Iris recalls the patient who died a year ago on her shift; she filed it 'unavoidable.' The machine later reveals she had a choice.
clues.note: Links past guilt to current mystery; payoff when truth shows she caused that death too.

clues.description: A second slip prints another patient's name and time after Iris tries to warn Lena's father. The patient dies at the printed time despite Iris's efforts.
clues.note: Shows that trying to intervene directly may not change the outcome; plants doubt that the machine can be outrun. Payoff when Iris's resistance in ch4-5 causes death.
